clue.text: Pronouncements of a recorder without a phone :

indicators.note: without tells us to take the word phone away from the recorder's name

parts.note: a Dictaphone is a trade-name office dictation recorder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to note down official statements with a dictating machine that has no telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta are authoritative statements, the plural of dictum, so pronouncements is a synonym.

clue.text: Postponement of French agitation

parts.note: de is French for of
ferment is a state of unrest or agitation

explanation.surface: The French delay a decision amid public unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferment is a delay, putting something off until later.

clue.text: Be of value as a nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone aims to be worth something as an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to matter or have worth; a count is a European noble ranking alongside an earl.

clue.text: Daughter of Cassiopeia and an Italian attorney?

parts.note: taken as written
Rome stands for something Italian; the question mark flags the loose link, a lawyer from Rome
DA is a district attorney, the American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A mythical princess is listed alongside a lawyer from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'an Italian attorney' as a Rome DA, a prosecutor of that city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda, chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus, was the child of Queen Cassiopeia.

clue.text: Flourished like Mérimée

explanation.surface: A French writer is said to have thrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Prosper Mérimée was the French author of Carmen; to be 'like him' is to be Prosper-ed, as bearded means having a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive or do well; and someone given the first name of Mérimée could be said to be Prosper-ed.

clue.text: "That poor man that hangs on —— favours!" (Henry VIII)

definitions.text: "That poor man that hangs on —— favours!" (Henry VIII)

parts.words: "That poor man that hangs on —— favours!" (Henry VIII)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Wolsey's farewell speech in Shakespeare, the missing word being royal sons

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare on the misery of depending on royal patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolsey in Henry VIII says 'O, how wretched is that poor man that hangs on princes' favours!'
explanation.definitionFit: Royal sons are the people whose patronage Wolsey laments depending on in the speech.

clue.text: Instrumental branch' of chemistry ?

explanation.surface: A question about a musical side of science.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic can describe something made by a church keyboard instrument; organic chemistry studies carbon compounds.

clue.text: Walker to sum up' when rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to recap is to summarise

explanation.surface: A hiker is asked to summarise the route on getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse or person that paces, walking with measured steps.

clue.text: An opulent place in. France for the cardinal

parts.note: riche is French for rich or opulent
lieu is French for place

explanation.surface: A wealthy spot in France is chosen for a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells you to put 'opulent place' into French: riche lieu.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was chief minister to Louis XIII of France.

clue.text: Draw off 500 on water transport

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a raft is a simple floating craft

explanation.surface: Drawing off five hundred people onto boats.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft is to draw off or select people or liquid for a purpose.

clue.text: Deserted child came across "the heather

parts.note: to come across something is to find it
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: An abandoned infant is discovered out on the moor among the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is an infant abandoned by its parents and found by others.

clue.text: After centuries alternating with ducks a drink is 'needed

indicators.note: after places the single letter at the end, following the alternating string

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for a century, a hundred runs in cricket
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O
a second century gives another C
a second duck gives another O

explanation.surface: A cricketer who has swung between big scores and noughts deserves a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternating with' interleaves two Cs (centuries) and two Os (ducks) to make COCO; 'After' puts A behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Endless allowance for a relation

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the allowance word is cut off

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or goods

explanation.surface: Someone is given a limitless allowance for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the proportional relation between two quantities.

clue.text: Agreeing to study urgent distribution

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: distribution means the letters of urgent are spread around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A student agrees to read about an urgent matter of sharing out supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges URGENT into GRUENT, placed after CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent means in agreement or harmony, so it can replace agreeing.

clue.text: Train daily

explanation.surface: Someone trains every day.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train with few stops; the Daily Express is a British national newspaper, a daily.

clue.text: He can't be, accused of spinelessness

definitions.text: He can't be, accused of spinelessness

parts.words: He can't be, accused of spinelessness
parts.note: spinelessness here means having no quills, and a quilled rodent is the one creature it cannot describe

explanation.surface: A man of strong character is praised for backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a rodent covered in sharp spines, so it is literally never spineless.

clue.text: Join company doctor in Egyptian capital

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree standing for a doctor
taken as written

indicators.note: capital here means the capital, or first, letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A firm's medic is told to sign up while staying in Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian capital' looks like Cairo, but 'capital' only asks for the first letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine is to bring things together, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Beggar acknowledging his incorrigibility

explanation.surface: A tramp admits he can never be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'Mend? I can't', the reply of someone admitting he cannot reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is a person who lives by begging; split up it reads as a refusal to reform.

clue.text: Whereby we get in trouble with ten cranes

indicators.note: trouble suggests the ten cranes are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten birds or machines cause us bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrances are the doors or gateways through which people go inside.

clue.text: Latin land in English land

parts.note: terra is the Latin word for land or earth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin word for land sits inside an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal: it gives the letters IN after TERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is the English word for a stretch of ground and its physical features.

clue.text: Perceives the section in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters of section are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sees that a department is in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or become aware of something, so perceives fits.

clue.text: Bar the end of the croquet dinner

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it

indicators.note: the end of the game's name means only its back part is kept, the front dropped

explanation.surface: A sports club bars the close of a croquet supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is an elaborate formal dinner for many guests.

clue.text: Haggle over lawyers profit

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
gain is a synonym for profit

explanation.surface: Arguing about how much money the legal profession makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to negotiate over the terms of a sale.

clue.text: Musical swan

parts.note: a swan species named after a brass player, whose call sounds like a blaring horn

explanation.surface: A swan that can sing.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpeter is a large North American swan whose call resembles a brass horn; a player of that horn bears the same name.

clue.text: Clever to, climb into these vehicles

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: smart means clever

explanation.surface: A bright person gets into a set of buses.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are streetcars, passenger vehicles running on rails.

clue.text: Body of men found in' possession:

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A gang is caught with stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group of people summoned by a sheriff to help.

clue.text: Some tricky work with rope here

definitions.text: Some tricky work with rope here

parts.words: Some tricky work with rope here
parts.note: points to the famous trick in which a fakir's rope rises into the air and a boy climbs it, named after a country

explanation.surface: A sailor does clever knots somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian rope trick is the legendary illusion said to be performed in that subcontinent.

clue.text: Avian admiral

explanation.surface: A bird-like naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, a bird; Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan admiral.

clue.text: Wrong a girl

parts.note: miss is a word for a young girl or unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone has wronged a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means faulty or not right, as in 'something is amiss'.

clue.text: Chance almost gets the horse inside the coach

indicators.note: inside means the horse goes within the shortened word
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A bettor's luck nearly runs out when a racehorse is loaded into the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CHANCE to CHANC; 'inside' puts ARAB within it after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Writer sounds as if, he delivered a rocket

indicators.note: sounds as if says the name is spoken and matches another of the same sound

parts.note: George Stephenson built the Rocket, a pioneering steam locomotive

explanation.surface: An author seems to have dispatched a firework or missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rocket was the 1829 locomotive of George Stephenson; Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island, has a surname pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Rows which cause weeping, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word spoken that matches another in sound

parts.note: tears are the drops that come with weeping

explanation.surface: Arguments that make people cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' tempts as quarrels, which can cause weeping; it means lines stacked one above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or layers placed one above the other, as in a stadium.
